_comment: English body for adobe-acrobat-ai; generated from the Chinese dossier and official pages, not a literal translation.

axes.model_access: Driven by Adobe’s generative document capabilities; the product page does not publish a full model list. Features vary by Acrobat tier.
axes.runtime: Runs in Acrobat web, desktop and mobile; document parsing and generation happen in Adobe’s cloud.
axes.local_files: Can read uploaded PDFs and documents and produce summaries, answers and citations; a local file must be opened in Acrobat or uploaded.
axes.background: Single-document Q&A and summaries return immediately; there is no long-running agent that survives shutdown. Tasks are triggered per request and no resident agent remains; long work must be split into reviewable steps.
axes.tools: Integrated with Acrobat PDF editing, signing, export and sharing; answers can be tied to page numbers in the source.
axes.context: Context is mainly the current PDF and conversation; cross-document knowledge-base capability is limited. Cross-document and cross-session memory is limited, so complex work needs manual context and source citations.
axes.permissions: Documents may contain sensitive information; confirm cloud storage and retention terms before processing. Commercial use follows the Adobe contract.
axes.fit: Fits: long-PDF summaries, contract clause location and document Q&A. Does not fit: replacing legal advice, financial audit or complex table calculation.

runs: This site has not completed measured task runs for this entry. We checked the official product, help and terms pages and recorded capabilities, data paths and known limits. Suggested checks: the real tier boundaries, the data-retention default, and one end-to-end task with representative content.

- Accuracy on scanned, handwritten and complex-table PDFs (not measured)
related: Both are document-AI products; Acrobat AI is tied to PDF workflows, while ChatPDF-style tools are lighter upload-and-ask surfaces.
Acrobat AI and Google Gemini in Drive both summarise documents; compare citation quality and enterprise retention terms.
Acrobat AI and Docling overlap on document parsing; Acrobat is a hosted product, Docling is an open-source parsing toolkit.
